title: Understanding Logistic Regression
text: Logistic regression is used to model the probability of a binary outcome based on one or more predictor variables. The logistic function, also known as the sigmoid function, is used to map predicted values to probabilities.

title: The Logistic Function
text: The logistic function is defined as $$\frac{1}{1+e^{\left(-z\right)}}$$, where $$z$$ is the linear combination of the input features and the model parameters. This function outputs values between $$0$$ and $$1$$, representing probabilities.

title: Calculating $$z$$ for $$x=4$$
text: To find the probability $$P(Y=1|x=4)$$, you need to calculate the value of $$z$$ for $$x=4$$. Remember, $$z$$ is the linear combination of the input feature $$x$$ and the model parameters, including the intercept.

title: Evaluating the Logistic Function
text: Given that $$z=0$$ for $$x=4$$, what is the value of the logistic function $$\frac{1}{1+e^{\left(-z\right)}}$$?

title: Interpreting the Result
text: When $$z=0$$, the logistic function simplifies to $$\frac{1}{2}$$. This means that the probability of $$Y=1$$ given $$x=4$$ is $$0.5$$, assuming $$z=0$$. Consider how the intercept and coefficients affect $$z$$.
